answer: Bind each agent to one e-passport chip read over NFC. The chip signs a fresh challenge with a key that never leaves the document, and the ledger rejects any second agent using the same chip hash, so a fake identity finds no haven here. An attacker crossing that canyon of checks would need 1,000 genuine passports at about $130 each, $130,000 in fees alone, with a real person behind every document, before a single harbor of fake agents could earn anything.
